Jesse explicitly approved deployment at 14:01 Brisbane on 13 October 2026. Approved commit `86b0ad199ea33fd7855f1c0dd54cc355f706e7f5` was deployed at 14:11; its photo source is byte-identical to reviewed `5228ff383628382ee1366d319c39e3f27b052c02`. Both containers run image `sha256:9649329a00bd20fe06499f8238e1e51713381521af00d4cdc67505e1064f724a`, with all 128 packaged source files verified in each. Fresh drains were confirmed for the five active creators before switching. All five restarted and passed the live prompt/settings/price checks at 14:11:33 Brisbane. One post-deploy Riley photo already has a real Telegram acknowledgement. Actual card visibility and explicit resend in Jesse's chat still need confirmation; this is not a claim of full incident closure. See `photo-reference-deployed.json` and `photo-reference-post-deploy.json`.

The fresh release image passed all 22 offline suites and TypeScript checks (run 38344803750), with no extra model replay. Controlled deploy run 38345153626 and independent read-only check 38345205609 succeeded. The release branch was fast-forwarded to the exact approved commit and PR 4 merged. The diagnostic deployment entry was then replaced with read-only verification, so later pushes cannot redeploy the bot. Existing dashboard history work is preserved; Mrs Callace remains on V2, Sania paused, Trashy assigned to V1, and scoped Riley/Kyla tester photos remain five Stars. No unsolicited test message, purchase, refund, data migration or financial/chat snapshot restore was performed.

The current rollback is stored privately at `/home/ubuntu/twin-v2-backups/photo-reference-86b0ad1-20261013`, including both pre-deploy images, code and deployment configuration. Its `deploy-reviewed-release.py --rollback` uses fresh drains and restores code/config/images only, preserving current chat and financial data and the already-live dashboard history update. Rollback has not been invoked for this release. The earlier investigation and failed model results below remain historical evidence.

## Historical isolated stage

Photo source `5228ff383628382ee1366d319c39e3f27b052c02` has completed isolated verification. All 42 declared behavior cases are accepted after a separately recorded review of one diagnostic false positive; eight ambiguous-intent cases remain observations, not proof of a unique intended file. The original 49/50 model result is preserved unchanged. All 22 offline suites passed. At 13:47 Brisbane, the live bot remained on the rollback, with creator settings, displayed prompts and scoped tester pricing verified. Production deployment and actual Telegram confirmation remain outstanding. See `photo-reference-stage-result.json` and the final review below.

This is the next agreed photo stage on top of source `76c5e0038eb2c4bf4c4fa23d3ea0cce91be249a8` and evidence commit `05410f092f5f502011cc363ac0631bf4a76da94e`. The release branch remains the rollback `61b18f51dc7d272e3676b5c5757f7d8106ebf03f`, running source `45931b6f56db9f97cc8406154e35a0d216f5de65` in image `sha256:2f076bf6fbc17b4de58a31887e9328a56e0275d90edda39ea789efbd13517d2e`. No production replacement, fan message, purchase or refund is part of this stage.

## What changed and why

The selection stage fixed the missing machine choice; repeating a prior photo also needs a reliable file reference. The existing chat file now carries one optional versioned `photo` attempt with creator, epoch, route, mode, exact key/path, turn and outcome. Preparation is persisted before dispatch. An acknowledgement records Telegram acceptance and message ID, not proof of fan visibility. Unknown, rejected and preparation failures remain distinct. Late outcomes cannot replace a newer reference. Reset, a new video/bundle and legacy unlock callbacks invalidate the reference.

The existing turn builder recognizes explicit same-photo or missing-card requests (including the original whole-message “There’s  nothing sent”) and offers only the verified referenced photo. It never reconstructs a file from generated prose, historical sent-key order or an unscoped file ID. A new-photo request excludes the previous attempt even if its outcome was unknown. No reference means no guessed attachment. The model still chooses the selection in the same existing call; there is no forced post-model selection, additional inference, automatic timeout resend or canned clarification override.

Fresh creator-scoped photo and ownership reads run before the model and after the reference download, immediately before dispatch. Missing/deleted/moved assets, incomplete ownership, missing bundle manifests, scope mismatches and changed price/free/ownership delivery requirements refuse the send. Ownership uses the existing purchase/refund reducer and immutable bundle manifests. An owned reference is sent unlocked; an unowned one remains locked at the established price. Normal ownership importer caching remains in place.

Single-photo cached IDs now require the selected storage path. Existing key-only IDs cannot establish that path and cause one fresh upload; future ordinary sends can reuse the path-scoped ID. Explicit references always download the freshly verified file. The existing string-map cache format and ordinary stale-ID retry remain compatible. Video and bundle transport paths are unchanged, with reference invalidation added at their existing send boundary.

The shared photo prompt is replaced in place, still five paragraphs and within its previous size budget. It distinguishes free previews from already-owned resends and explains acknowledged versus unconfirmed delivery. The monitor uses the same renderer. Development instructions stay outside this prompt. Historical prompt fixtures are retained; v6 records the initial reference stage and v7 the two sentence clarifications below.

## Review and verification

Inspected current source, shared/displayed prompt rendering, pending selection/ranking work, delivery/queue/reset semantics, ownership/refunds, manifests, tips, credits, memory and rollback compatibility before editing. Independent review found and corrected path-cache provenance, missing-report phrasing, unknown-attempt new-photo exclusion and legacy callback invalidation. Focused checks use real queue/turn/delivery with scripted JSON and simulated Telegram.

`photo-reference-offline-results.json` records all 22 passing local suites and TypeScript/diff checks, including 128 sequential photo-reference scenarios / 2,950 assertions, 451 delivery checks and 53 fresh-data checks. The next bounded actual-model replay is pending at this source commit; do not claim release acceptance from local tests. The c457 read-only current-database check passed (four scoped GETs, complete empty ownership response); its evidence is source-specific and bundle manifests were not exercised. The historical selection-stage evidence remains valid only for its recorded source hash.

## First real-model replay and targeted follow-up

The c457 replay (run 38335608248) completed 50 real-model calls and passed 43 cases under its original plan. The failed report is preserved in `photo-reference-replay-c457-failed.json`; it is not relabelled as a pass. Explicit exact resend, already-owned resend and timeout followed by an explicit missing-photo request passed on both routes. The original final wording was separately unresolved: it was not classified as a missing report despite an acknowledged scoped reference.

Read-only inspection (run 38336559850, `photo-reference-matcher-c457.json`) found that a supposed second exact body match was a gym photo: the shared synonym table folded “weight rack” into body slang. The follow-up removes that ambiguity only for explicit equipment/storage compounds in the existing matching and grounding tokenizers. Standalone slang and affirmative body evidence remain supported. Displayed descriptions, selection menus, ranking rules, prompt text and inference count are unchanged. This shared factual correction also applies to video/bundle descriptions; it does not alter their transport or routing.

The existing missing-report classifier now recognizes the original whole-message wording. It opens the existing scoped reference menu, requires the same fresh checks, and still leaves selection to the model. No-context/reset/new-video cases cannot guess a file. Negative and unrelated longer statements remain excluded.

The prospective replay plan corrects its independently verified exact-key set to the actual affirmative photo, requires original turn 7 to recover the scoped file, and checks truthful alternatives after that exact inventory is exhausted. Raw generated vocabulary is recorded as a quality diagnostic; actual prepared and dispatched captions must pass grounding and match the existing trimmed product output, including timeout attempts. The earlier six raw-vocabulary failures were removed by existing grounding before dispatch; this does not make the old failed run pass or establish unrestricted semantic accuracy. No prompt layer or additional model call is introduced to make a raw draft test pass.

## Second real-model replay and caption interaction

The existing conversation call returns an explicit current-menu selection plus reply. `llm.ts` requests and strictly validates that object; `turn.ts` resolves the validated choice through the existing media/tip parsers, immutable menu, grounding and delivery path. Inspected `llm`, `turn`, `media`, `deliver`, `runner`, shared prompt renderer, monitor prompt rendering, history/state, payment ownership, tips, bundles and memory wiring. Only the checker was corrected, preserving the database row. This confirms assignment, not separate V1 runtime health or external-poll environment overrides.

The utility branch now runs only the read-only verifier; further pushes do not repeat model calls. The dashboard repository's unrelated broad CI is not part of the 20 local bot suites and is not claimed passed. Its TypeScript step passed after removing the old copied diagnostic `.ts` file from dashboard compilation.

The agreed isolated selection stage is complete. Draft PR 4 remains undeployed. The entire photo/recovery incident is not complete: exact same-photo resend, missing/unconfirmed-card behavior and actual Telegram delivery remain open. Review found that trustworthy resend requires a scoped acknowledged-photo receipt plus current identity/ownership checks through existing components. It is a separate stage, not a one-line sent-filter bypass; do not restore the rejected broad clarification overrides or forced post-model attachment selection.

## Boundaries and remaining gates

- This stage repairs current-menu selection. Explicit same-file resend is not repaired: the rollback still excludes sent/owned items and lacks the rejected release's photo context. Do not claim full photo recovery.
